description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Mr. Smarak Swain explores how the concept of trust is being transformed in an age shaped by artificial intelligence. Drawing from his experiences in taxation, financial investigations, and public policy, he examines the evolution of Know Your Customer (KYC) systems and why they remain critical in protecting individuals and institutions from fraud.

Through real-world examples of cybercrime, mule accounts, identity theft, and AI-generated deepfakes, he reveals how rapidly advancing technology is challenging traditional methods of verification. As digital impersonation becomes increasingly sophisticated, he argues that trust can no longer be taken for granted and that verification is becoming a personal responsibility as much as an institutional one.

Connecting the history of KYC with emerging AI-driven threats, Smarak highlights the importance of digital awareness, critical thinking, and informed skepticism in navigating an increasingly complex wor
title: From Know Your Customer to Know Your Reality in the Age of AI | Mr. Smarak Swain | TEDxKPRCAS

author: TEDx Talks
description: From a small city in South India, Venkatesh has spent 27 years turning curiosity into companies. Inspired by his grandfather who built a textile empire at 60, he chose a different path, founding an IT company when the internet was still a novelty, then building and exiting ventures like Galatta and Magzter. But his real subject is the mindset behind it all. Drawing on a life that spans 100+ countries, Rotary service, and a decade of angel investing, he argues that change-makers aren't defined by big ideas but by a sharper eye: the ability to see the pain point everyone else overlooks, and the courage to build before the world catches up. He is  based in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. He founded Dot Com Infoway in 1999, building a digital services company that today with customers across 40+ countries, and co-founded Magzter, the global digital newsstand. He currently leads Simbli.ai, osmAPI, and 916 Studio, an AI-native vertical entertainment venture producing socially conscious micro-dramas.
title: Madurai Roots, Bold Ideas, Lasting Impact | Venkatesh Rajendran (CRV) | TEDxKharadi Salon

Rajmohan challenges the way we approach children's success. He argues that in our obsession with early achievement and academic performance, we neglect something fundamental , movement, exploration, and play , and that this neglect has consequences that show up years later. His talk introduces the concept of Movement Literacy and makes the case that before 12, the goal should not be winning but building the body and brain that can eventually choose.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Tarra Ajwani challenges how we define talent in an increasingly global workforce. What if identity isn’t something to overcome in professional spaces, but something to leverage?  Drawing from her experience living and working between India and the United States, she reframes intersectionality as a strategic superpower in the creative industries. 

Tarra reflects on years of adaptive code-switching, only to realize that the outlier identity she once tried to downplay was her greatest professional advantage. She argues that living between cultures, disciplines, or systems builds a rare kind of fluency - the ability to translate, bridge, and innovate. Tarra is an emerging music industry strategist working at the intersection of culture, storytelling, media, and marketing through a global lens. Raised in Mumbai, India, and driven by a desire to support artists through business strategy, she was led across the world to Berklee College of Music’s inaugural Music Industry Leadership and Inno
title: The outsider advantage | Tarra Ruchee Ajwani | TEDxBerklee Boston

description:
Drawing on psychology and neuroscience, as well as his experience helping artists connect with audiences worldwide, Fernando reveals how music taps into the deepest parts of our human experience. Rhythm resonates with life itself, beginning with the heartbeat in the womb. Melody shapes our identity and personal expression. Harmony creates familiarity and a sense of belonging, often predicting popularity. Lyrics become part of our sentimental heritage, linking songs to the moments of our lives. 

Through live music, storytelling, and science-backed insights, this talk reveals that the songs we love are more than entertainment, they carry our emotions, memories, and identity, showing that music isn’t just something we hear, but something we become. Fernando Gabriel is the Founder and CEO of Strm Music, an AI-powered platform revolutionizing music intelligence for artists and labels worldwide. With over 20 years of experience as a singer, songwriter, entrepreneur, and investor, Fernando
title: Is Old Music Better? | Fernando Gabriel | TEDxBerklee Boston

description: E se pausar não fosse parar, mas um ato de coragem? Nesta palestra, Klebér Tani compartilha sua experiência com a Meditação Transcendental e mostra como o silêncio e a consciência podem se tornar ferramentas poderosas para equilibrar a mente, reduzir o excesso de estímulos e fortalecer a clareza nas decisões. Um convite para desacelerar em um mundo que não para. O professor Klebér Tani tem sessenta e cinco anos, conheceu a técnica de Meditação Transcendental aos 17. Aos vinte anos, saiu do Brasil para se tornar professor de Meditação Transcendental com o monge e físico Maharishi Mahesh Yogi. Ao longo do tempo que esteve ensinando a MT profissionalmente, teve a oportunidade de ministrar cursos para mais de trinta mil pessoas. Após  se formar como educador físico, trabalhou no mestrado e pós graduação da universidade Gama Filho. Nesse período treinou atletas de alto rendimento, criou uma área de trabalho chamada de fisiologia do repouso, onde passou anos estudando a importância da volta
title: A Meditação Transcendental e a coragem de pausar | Klebér Tani | TEDxCarandá

I'm thirteen. And I look at school and wonder: what world is it preparing us for?

Marco has spent two years watching artificial intelligence go from a curious toy to a tool capable of writing essays, solving problems, and improving its own code. If answers are everywhere, what's the point of school still testing our ability to memorise them?

In this talk, Marco isn't here to complain about technology. He's here to propose something harder: changing what we understand by learning. Less "repeat and don't make mistakes." More "think, verify, build." Because his generation doesn't just need to adapt to the future. It needs to shape it. Marco is a 13-year-old Italian and Spanish student with excellent academic performance, maintaining an average of 9.5 out of 10. He speaks Italian, Spanish, and English fluently, and is also studying Chinese. author: TEDx Talks
description:
En 1917, en Chicago, un vendedor de seguros (Melvin Jones) tuvo una idea. Un simple aleteo, en principio. Poca gente le prestó atención. Nadie imaginó lo que desencadenaría.

Porque las ideas no viajan solas. Necesitan personas que las crean, que las impulsen, que las lleven más lejos de lo que su creador imaginó. Y esta idea viajó mucho: cruzó océanos, atravesó fronteras, cambió de manos una y otra vez, hasta llegar a un pueblo de Extremadura, Zafra.
 
Décadas después, gracias a ese efecto en cadena, un hombre que nació ciego (Antolín) pudo ver.

Darío Martínez y su hijo (también Darío) trazan la línea invisible que conecta Chicago con Zafra, un sueño con una vida transformada, y una generación con la siguiente. 

Y nos dejan una pregunta: ¿y tú? ¿qué aleteo vas a provocar? Darío is a 17-year-old International Baccalaureate student at CIS-San Francisco de Paula. Born and raised in Seville, he has also spent years abroad in Sacramento, USA and Melbourne, Australia. Passionate about En
title: El aleteo de Melvin | Darío Martínez de Azcona Morán & Darío Martínez de Azcona | TEDxCIS SFP Youth

description:
Rahul opens with a confession: he has been doing politics his entire life, and so has everyone in the room. His talk reframes politics not as elections or parliament, but as the art of navigating human relationships, the hesitation before you speak, the calculation in every conversation, the silence that costs more than it saves. Drawing on Chanakya, the ancient Indian strategist and philosopher, and on Krishna, Shakuni, and Dhritarashtra from the Indian epic the Mahabharata, he makes the case that silence is not neutral. It is always a choice, and it always has a price.
